subject: Oceanography
title: History of Ocean Exploration
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: History of Ocean Exploration.

hook.text: In 1872, HMS Challenger sailed for three years and discovered over 4,000 new species—modern oceanography was born.

buildup.text: Before Challenger, the deep ocean was thought lifeless—a dark, empty void.

discovery.text: The expedition measured depths, temperatures, and currents across all major oceans.

twist.text: Challenger found life at every depth tested—shattering the 'azoic theory' of a dead deep sea.

climax.text: Its 50 volumes of published results took 23 years to complete and filled 29,500 pages.

punchline.text: One ship, three years—and oceanography was born.

quiz.question: What did the HMS Challenger expedition prove?
options: Life exists at every ocean depth
Currents don't exist in deep water
